one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 2026 results are listed for Nov 4, 2026 after the close (MarketBeat; the company's own date announcement is not out yet, Q2's came on Jul 1 for an Aug 5 print), and the Talbot lead-plaintiff deadline is Nov 16. Both fall after Oct 31. Inside the window: the company's earnings-date announcement, pre-earnings previews, and a steady stream of alternative-data reads (Wells Fargo traffic-weighted Pixel installs, Citi/Store Leads merchant counts, Sensor Tower ad-network share, Unity commentary). Single notes have moved the stock 3-5% a day (Edgewater on Sep 23, Wells Fargo on Sep 30). These cut both ways, and the stock is at a fresh 52-week low after a 60% drawdown, where momentum and short-term reversal roughly offset each other. I stay symmetric around $281.31 with a monthly sigma of about 20% (75% annual realized vol / 3.5 is about 21%) and take no directional view; unchanged from round 1 because nothing the supervisor found falls inside the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (FY27 EPS $19.0, consensus $20.00 cut 5%, x 18x = $342), EV/EBITDA (FY27 revenue $10.0B x 81% = $8.1B x 12x, less $0.46B net debt, / 330M shares = $293) and FCF yield (FY27 FCF ~$6.2B at 6.5%, less net debt, / 330M = $286), weighted 40/30/30, gives about $310.

inputs_detail.value: $20.00 (27 analysts; $21.16 sixty days ago; 19 down vs 5 up revisions in 30 days)

inputs_detail.derivation: Cut consensus by 5% (was 7.5% in round 1). Edgewater's Q4 call (+8-9% q/q, ~$2.25B) is only ~1-2% below consensus revenue, so the near-term gap is small; the rest of the haircut reflects Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted Pixel data (~85% of new sites with no traffic, e-commerce 'more like a 2027 story') and still-negative revisions. Fits the supervisor's 3-5% range at its upper end because Unity Vector's 23% q/q growth adds spread pressure.

The market pays about 14x FY27 consensus ($281/$20). Growth is still ~25-30% (FY27 revenue $10.26B vs FY26 $8.10B), net debt is negligible and the SEC probe is closed; the class action, AI-model execution miss and Unity competition cap the multiple far below the 30x+ history. 18x on FY27 is about 15-16x on the NTM EPS the market will look at in Oct 2027, close to large-cap ad peers.

TIKR puts NTM levered FCF yield at ~6% today; I require a bit more given the execution and legal overhang.

bear.story: The e-commerce/self-serve push stalls, as the traffic-weighted Pixel data suggests (most new sites are dormant APAC storefronts; Shopify app has only 25 reviews at 3.6 stars, with region-availability complaints). Edgewater's 'share ceiling' proves right and Unity Vector (+23% q/q in Q2) compresses AppLovin's spreads. FY27 EPS ~$15.5 and the multiple compresses to ~11x. (The Muddy Waters short report and SEC probe are dropped as drivers: the probe closed with no action.)

base.story: Gaming stays dominant (~36% of mobile game ad revenue, iOS share rising). Model upgrades live since Q2 bring growth near guidance; Q4 grows ~8-10% q/q; e-commerce scales slowly through 2027. FY27 EPS ~$19 and the market holds a mid-to-high-teens multiple while class actions linger.

bull.story: Q3/Q4 beat on model improvements, the generative video tool ships, and holiday web advertiser cohorts show real traffic-weighted traction. Revisions turn up, FY27 EPS $20-21+, and the stock re-rates toward 23-25x, as APP itself did in 2023 and Meta did in 2023 once revisions turned. Inside this case the tail reaches $600-700+.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $180 (~9x FY27 consensus EPS, ~9.5x my $19, and roughly a 10% FCF yield with negligible net debt), the price would most likely mean the earnings base itself is breaking, not just the multiple: a Q4 guide implying flat or negative sequential growth in the core gaming business, clear share loss to Unity Vector or Meta, platform action against data practices, or e-commerce cohorts churning. The fall from $738 to $281 is explained by de-rating plus a modest growth reset; a further ~36% drop is not, without a fundamental problem. Raised from $175 because the haircut EPS base is higher and the regulatory tail is smaller (SEC probe closed).

reasoning: Round 2. Hard facts unchanged: Q2 2026 revenue $1.92B (+53%), 84% EBITDA margin, Q3 guide $2.055-2.085B, net debt ~$0.46B, ~337M diluted shares, ~14x FY27 consensus EPS at $281. Supervisor findings I accepted: (1) Edgewater's Q4 call is only ~1-2% below consensus, so my 7.5% EPS haircut was too deep; I moved to 5%, at the upper end of the supervisor's 3-5% because I add Unity Vector's 23% q/q Q2 growth (Unity release, confirmed by trade press) as a spread-pressure factor the supervisor did not weight. (2) My right tail was too thin; I widened the scenario inner sigmas to 38/30/40% and lifted the bull price to $490, which raises P(>=563) from 0.06 to 0.10 and P(>=703) from 0.014 to 0.048, consistent with APP's own 2023 rebound and Meta 2023. (3) Muddy Waters and the SEC probe removed from the bear story. Kept: the Wells Fargo traffic-weighted Pixel work as the key alt-data read (the supervisor rated it the most decision-useful finding); a new in-lane check of the Shopify App Store listing (25 reviews, 3.6 stars, latest Sep 15 2026, complaints about region availability) fits the view that self-serve e-commerce is early and small. Fair value rises from $302 to $310 (P/E $342, EV/EBITDA $293, FCF yield $286). I stay a bit below the supervisor's ~$320 because revisions are still falling and Unity competition is accelerating. Mixture: bear $170/25%, base $315/50%, bull $490/25%, which gives a median near $308 and P(>=281) of 0.58. The 1-month ladder is unchanged (no earnings before Nov 4). Research in round 2: 7 searches/fetches; X and Reddit were not reached directly, and a reported Oct 2 price move after a Unity spokesperson's comments was not used (after the as-of date and not verified).
